welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
a person is standing eighteen meter away from a pole.
The person's eye level is one point five meter above the ground,
and the angle of elevation from the eye to the top of the pole
is forty-five degrees.
We need to find the full height of the pole.
Let us take the height from the person's eye level to the top of the pole as
x meter.
Why are we taking only this upper part?
Because the angle of elevation starts from the person's eye,
not from the ground.
Now, look at the right triangle.
The horizontal distance between the person and the pole is eighteen meters, so this becomes the adjacent side.
The vertical height from the eye level to the top is x meter, so this becomes the opposite side.
Using the tan formula,
tan theta is equal to opposite divided by adjacent.
So tan forty-five degree is equal to x divided by eighteen.
We know that tan forty-five degree is equal to one, therefore one is equal to x divided by eighteen. This gives us x equal to eighteen meters.
Okay,
we have found the height of the pole above the person's eye level.
Are we done?
Not yet.
The question asks for the full height of the pole, so we must also add the person's eye level,
which is one point five meter.
The full height is eighteen plus one point
five, which is nineteen point five meter.
Hence, the height of the pole is nineteen point five meter. So the correct option is D.
